name: pstack-claude
description: Antigravity, Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Gemini, Muse, OpenCode, Pi, and Prime Agent versions of Poteto's pstack. Rigorous agent workflows with Cursor primitives translated for other harnesses.
readmeExcerpt:
# pstack Lauren Tan's [pstack](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack) is an opinionated Cursor skill stack that improves agent outcomes. This is a port for Claude Code, Codex, Pi, GitHub Copilot, Muse, and other agent harnesses. It tracks upstream and also carries named policy forks, each declared in [`tools/forks.json`](tools/forks.json). Tell `poteto-mode` your goal and it will invoke the correct workflow for the task. It keeps your code concise, simple and verified. For concurrency bugs and invariants that tests cannot reach, `/create-formal-verification-skill` picks the riskiest property in your code, verifies it with a tool that fits, and leaves a project skill the next agent reruns. The separate [agent-formal-verify](https://github.com/michael-denyer/agent-formal-verify) plugin goes deeper on the method, with guided TLA+ model checking, Lean proofs, and Kani for Rust. ## Built for Claude Code This port translates upstream's Cursor skills for Claude Code before installation. [Upstream's Claude Code install](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/c742dd6/harness/pstack/claude-code) asks agents to translate Cursor names at runtime, using extra tokens and relying on them to apply the mapping correctly. This port also adds a SessionStart hook that routes tasks to `poteto-mode`. ## Install
Claude Code Run in Claude Code 2.1.292 or later: ```text /plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude /plugin install pstack@pstack-claude ``` Claude Code leaves auto-update off for third-party marketplaces, so pstack stays on the version you installed. To turn it on, run `/plugin`, open the **Marketplaces** tab, select `pstack-claude`, and choose **Enable auto-update**. To update once by hand, run `claude plugin update pstack@pstack-claude`.
Codex Run in your terminal: ```shell codex plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude ``` Invoke a skill by typing `$` and its name, such as `$poteto-mode` or `$babysit`, then choosing its entry, which inserts `$pstack:`. `/skills` lists every skill.
Pi Run in your terminal: ```shell pi install git:github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude ``` The package loads the skills and the pstack Pi extension, which adds the subagent, question, and wake-up tools the skills use, plus `/loop` and the routing instruction. Invoke a skill with `/skill:`.
GitHub Copilot Run in your terminal: ```shell copilot plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude copilot plugin install pstack@pstack-claude ``` This installs pstack for the Copilot CLI and the GitHub Copilot app, which share `~/.copilot`. Start a new session afterwards. Copilot ships no default pstack models, so the first skill that needs one runs `setup-pstack` to pick from the models your account lists, and later sessions reuse that choice. The Copilot build is tested on Copilot CLI 1.0.87 through 1.0.92. On those versions the routing hook's context reaches the session alongside other plugins' session-start context. If a later version keeps only one plugin's context, `setup-pstack` offers a [standing instruction](plugins/pstack/skills/setup-pstack/copilot.md#wire-it-in) for `~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md` instead. On 1.0.92, once the CLI caches its computer-use experiment assignment, `copilot -p` sessions list no plugin skills and a `skill` call returns "Skill not found". Interactive sessions, the hooks, and the agents are unaffected.
Muse Run in your terminal: ```shell git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude cd pstack-claude muse plugins install ./plugins/pstack muse plugins approve pstack ``` The first command installs the native Muse plugin bundle. The second approves its `SessionStart` hook and agent definitions, which Muse runs only after approval. Start a new session afterwards. Invoke a skill with `/` (for example `/poteto-mode`), which Muse lists for each user-invocable skill.
OMP Run in your terminal: ```shell omp plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude omp plugin install --scope user pstack@pstack-claude ``` Restart OMP after installing, disabling, or uninstalling pstack. OMP 18.16.0 shares one plugin cache across scopes, so an upgrade or removal can affect other installations; inspect their source and scope before changing them. See [OMP issue 16827](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/issues/16827).
Kimi Code CLI After a release containing `kimi.plugin.json` is published, close other Kimi sessions and install it in a fresh Kimi Code CLI session: ```text /plugins install https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude /reload ``` To test an unreleased checkout, use `/plugins install /absolute/path/to/pstack-claude` instead, followed by `/reload`; Kimi copies the whole checkout, including Git metadata and local files, so use a clean, reviewed copy. To update, close other Kimi sessions, reinstall from the same source in a fresh session, and run `/reload`. Invoke a skill as `/skill:pstack:poteto-mode`; see the [Kimi mapping](plugins/pstack/skills/poteto-mode/references/kimi-tools.md) for tool guidance.
Grok Build ```shell git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude cd pstack-claude grok plugin install "$PWD/plugins/pstack" --trust grok plugin enable pstack ``` Start a new session and use `/poteto-mode` to load the skill explicitly. To update a local install, quit Grok sessions, inspect `grok plugin details pstack` and back up any edits in the installed copy, pull the checkout, run `grok plugin uninstall pstack --keep-data`, and repeat the last two commands. If pstack was disabled, disable it again before restarting. `grok plugin update` does not refresh a local install.
MiniMax Code For a first install, check that `${MINIMAX_DATA_DIR:-$HOME/.minimax}/plugins/pstack` does not already exist. Then run in your terminal: ```shell git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude cd pstack-claude mkdir -p "${MINIMAX_DATA_DIR:-$HOME/.minimax}/plugins" cp -R plugins/pstack "${MINIMAX_DATA_DIR:-$HOME/.minimax}/plugins/pstack" ``` MiniMax Code loads each directory under `plugins/` in its data directory as a local plugin, and reads pstack through its Claude Code reader with the skills, agents, and routing hook. `mcode plugin list` shows it as `pstack@local`. To update, record its enabled state, quit every `mcode` process, and move `plugins/pstack` to an unused path outside `plugins/`. Run `git pull` and the `cp` line again. Check `mcode plugin list` and restore the previous enabled state if needed.
OpenCode 2 Clone the repository, then add the absolute path to `plugins/pstack/opencode` to the existing `plugins` array in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`. On Windows, use a path such as `C:/Users/name/pstack-claude/plugins/pstack/opencode`. Restart OpenCode after checkout updates. Alternatively, install, check, or update the native Git package: ```bash opencode plugin add 'github:michael-denyer/pstack-claude#main' opencode plugin check 'github:michael-denyer/pstack-claude#main' opencode plugin update 'github:michael-denyer/pstack-claude#main' ``` A commit-pinned reference does not advance. If a check immediately after installation reports no package plugins, wait for the server to load it and check again. If you previously installed pstack skills into `~/.agents/skills`, inspect the links and remove only those pointing to your pstack checkout before using the plugin. The plugin registers `pstack-` skill IDs and adds routing in root sessions. If routing is missing, run `opencode api get /api/skill` and check that each `pstack-` path belongs to this plugin. Resolve any conflicting skill before manually invoking that ID. Use `session hook: off` in the OpenCode model sheet to disable routing. To remove the plugin, remove its configured path and restart the service, or use `opencode plugin remove` with the exact Git specifier. OpenCode 1 is unsupported. See the [OpenCode mapping](plugins/pstack/skills/poteto-mode/references/opencode-tools.md).
Antigravity (agy) Run in your terminal: ```shell git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude cd pstack-claude agy plugin install ./plugins/pstack ``` This installs the native Antigravity plugin bundle (`skills`, `agents`, and `SessionStart` routing hook) into `~/.gemini/config/plugins/pstack`.
Other harnesses Gemini CLI, Prime Agent, and skills-only Codex installs read skills from `~/.agents/skills/`. Run in your terminal: ```shell git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude cd pstack-claude mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills for s in plugins/pstack/skills/*/; do target=~/.agents/skills/"$(basename "$s")" test -e "$target" || test -L "$target" || ln -s "$(pwd)/$s" "$target" done ``` To update, run `git pull` in the clone, then run the `for` loop again to link skills added since the last run. These installs have no routing hook, so ask for `poteto-mode` by name or add a standing instruction to the harness's instruction file. See [shared installation](docs/reference.md#shared-skills-installation) for per-harness notes and uninstalling.
### Configure pstack provides automatic routing on Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Muse, MiniMax Code, Antigravity, Pi, Kimi Code CLI, OMP, and OpenCode 2. The runtimes deliver the instruction at different points: Kimi adds it while the plugin is enabled, OMP adds it before each main-agent turn, and OpenCode adds it at each model step in root sessions. Grok Build exposes a routing hint through a skill description; the model may not follow it. Codex requires hook trust through `/hooks`, and Muse requires `muse plugins approve pstack`. Other harnesses have no automatic routing. Run `setup-pstack` to turn automatic routing on or off, change model defaults, or set a reasoning effort per role (`arena runners: opus @xhigh, fable @max`). On OMP, the session hook setting applies globally across profiles; on Kimi, enable or disable the plugin to control routing. See the [routing reference](docs/reference.md#automatic-routing). ## Getting started ```text Use poteto-mode to fix the search filter resetting when I change pages. ``` For a bug, it reproduces the failure, uses `how` and `why` to investigate, delegates the fix, then reruns the failing case. If the fix crosses a function boundary, it brings in `architect` before implementation. You receive the fix and the failing and passing evidence. [Other playbooks](plugins/pstack/skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md#playbooks) cover planning, features, refactoring, performance issues, investigations, prototypes, PR maintenance, shipping, and longer projects. ## Details - [Skills and slash commands](docs/reference.md#slash-commands) - [Runtime setup](docs/reference.md#runtime-support) - [Models and dependencies](docs/reference.md#configuration-and-dependencies) - [Maintenance and port scope](docs/reference.md#maintenance) ## Data handling pstack has no server or telemetry. Anything its skills ask your agent to read, including session transcripts, goes to your model provider. Scripts run locally, and PR tools use your GitHub CLI login. ## Contributing Thanks for helping make this port better. Bug reports, documentation fixes, and runtime improve

`worktree-audit.mjs` now checks a worktree's ancestry against `refs/remotes/origin/<trunk>`. git resolves the shorthand `origin/<trunk>` to a tag or local branch of that name before the remote-tracking ref. Such a ref pointing at unmerged work made the audit report the worktree merged and safe. The REMOTE column's ahead count reads `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` for the same reason. @EthanYoQ found and fixed the trunk case in [#423](https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude/pull/423).

When a branch has several PRs, the audit now holds its worktree for an open one even when `gh` lists a newer closed or merged PR first. The first record listed used to decide, so a merged record at the worktree's head marked it safe while another PR from the branch was still open. @EthanYoQ fixed this in [#424](https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude/pull/424).

`setup-pstack`'s `SKILL.md` now covers the Claude Code path only, at 8,978 bytes instead of 17,690. The sheet-path table and each other runtime's step changes are in [`references/runtimes.md`](plugins/pstack/skills/setup-pstack/references/runtimes.md), which `SKILL.md` tells every other runtime to read first. Step 3 lets a role

`resume.mjs` now ignores links inside the fenced code blocks of a note saved with CRLF line endings, as its link rule says. The fence pattern's opening line ends in `.*\n`, and `.` does not match a carriage return. In a CRLF note the pattern missed each tilde fence, so `publish` read the links inside it and failed with `does not resolve (ENOENT)`. A leading byte order mark did the same to a fence on the note's first line. `verifyLinks` now strips the mark and folds CRLF to LF before it removes code, as `check-playbooks.mjs` does. The recorded sha256 does not change, because `fileInfo` hashes the file's bytes. @wattanartongtipsukon-create found and fixed the CRLF case in [#416](https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude/pull/416), and a follow-up commit on that PR added the byte order mark case.

The generator now writes the Platform Adaptation sentence in `poteto-mode/SKILL.md` from the rows of `RUNTIMES` in `tools/runtimes.mjs` (#413). It also writes each runtime mapping's list of diverse-model panel skills from the `panel` roles in `models.json` (#412). A new runtime or a role change no longer needs a hand edit to either. The one shipped text change drops "CLI or app," afte

The Model names section of every runtime mapping (`codex-tools.md`, `pi-tools.md`, `copilot-tools.md`, `muse-tools.md`, `minimax-tools.md`, `agy-tools.md`, and `grok.md`) named `how` critics and `reflect` as diverse-model panels. Only `arena`, `architect`, and `interrogate` have a role on the `panel` tier in `models.json`. The sync to upstream e8d856f (#67) retired the `how critics` role, and `reflect` never had a panel role. The mappings now name the three. `tests/models.test.mjs` compares each mapping's panel list with the skills that have a `panel` role, so a role change that leaves the list stale fails the test.

Three `grok.md` rows now match Grok Build's subagent guide (#410). `spawn_subagent` takes `run_in_background`, which defaults to true. `send_subagent_message` exists behind `GROK_ACTIVE_AGENT_MESSAGES` or `[features] active_agent_messages`. A dispatch for `general-purpose` or `pstack:poteto-agent` omits `subagent_type`, because Grok cannot select `general-purpose` by name and runs an omitted type as general-purpose.

pstack now installs as a native Kimi Code CLI plugin. The root [`kimi.plugin.json`](kimi.plugin.json) points Kimi at the shared skills tree and adds the routing instruction in [`kimi-instructions.md`](plugins/pstack/hooks/kimi-instructions.md) to the system prompt while the plugin is enabled. This is the first release that carries the manifest, which the README's Kimi install waits for. In a fresh session, run `/plugins install https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude` and `/reload`, and invoke a skill as `/skill:pstack:poteto-mode`. The new [`kimi-tools.md`](plugins/pstack/skills/poteto-mode/references/kimi-tools.md) maps Claude tools to Kimi's, with `Agent` and its built-in `coder`, `explore`, and `plan` agents, and `CronCreate` for a one-time wake-up. Kimi reads no `session hook` line, so `/plugins disable pstack` is how to turn routing off, and `setup-pstack` writes no effort or hook lines there. On Kimi Code CLI 2.4.1 for macOS, installation and delivery of routing and skill content to a synthetic provider were verified; model compliance is untested. @donbeave added Kimi support in [#394](https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude/pull/394).

pstack now loads as a

pstack now runs on Antigravity. `agy plugin install ./plugins/pstack` installs all 67 skills, the 4 agents, and the `SessionStart` routing hook from the new [`.antigravity-plugin/plugin.json`](plugins/pstack/.antigravity-plugin/plugin.json) and a root [`hooks.json`](plugins/pstack/hooks.json). Antigravity reads hooks only from that root file and ignores Claude Code's `hooks/hooks.json`. The hook runs `./hooks/session-start.sh agy`. Antigravity starts hooks in the installed plugin directory and sets no plugin-root variable, so the `agy` arm of the shared script uses paths relative to that directory. It emits the poteto-mode mandate as an `injectSteps` system message, and `session hook: off` in `~/.gemini/config/pstack-models.md` turns it off. The new [`agy-tools.md`](plugins/pstack/skills/poteto-mode/references/agy-tools.md) maps Claude tools to Antigravity's, with `invoke_subagent` and its `Model` values `inherit`, `flash_lite`, `flash`, and `pro`. Antigravity's native skill loader keeps only the first 24,000 bytes of a skill body, which drops the end of poteto-mode, so the mandate and the mapping tell the agent to read poteto-mode's `SKILL.md` in full with `read_file`.

pstack

Lauren Tan's pstack is an opinionated Cursor skill stack that improves agent outcomes. This is a port for Claude Code, Codex, Pi, GitHub Copilot, Muse, and other agent harnesses. It tracks upstream and also carries named policy forks, each declared in tools/forks.json.

Tell poteto-mode your goal and it will invoke the correct workflow for the task. It keeps your code concise, simple and verified.

For concurrency bugs and invariants that tests cannot reach, /create-formal-verification-skill picks the riskiest property in your code, verifies it with a tool that fits, and leaves a project skill the next agent reruns. The separate agent-formal-verify plugin goes deeper on the method, with guided TLA+ model checking, Lean proofs, and Kani for Rust.

Built for Claude Code

This port translates upstream's Cursor skills for Claude Code before installation. Upstream's Claude Code install asks agents to translate Cursor names at runtime, using extra tokens and relying on them to apply the mapping correctly. This port also adds a SessionStart hook that routes tasks to poteto-mode.

Install

Claude Code

Run in Claude Code 2.1.292 or later:

/plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude
/plugin install pstack@pstack-claude

Claude Code leaves auto-update off for third-party marketplaces, so pstack stays on the version you installed. To turn it on, run /plugin, open the Marketplaces tab, select pstack-claude, and choose Enable auto-update. To update once by hand, run claude plugin update pstack@pstack-claude.

Codex

Run in your terminal:

codex plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude
codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude

Invoke a skill by typing $ and its name, such as $poteto-mode or $babysit, then choosing its entry, which inserts $pstack:<name>. /skills lists every skill.

Pi

Run in your terminal:

pi install git:github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude

The package loads the skills and the pstack Pi extension, which adds the subagent, question, and wake-up tools the skills use, plus /loop and the routing instruction. Invoke a skill with /skill:<name>.

GitHub Copilot

Run in your terminal:

copilot plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude
copilot plugin install pstack@pstack-claude

This installs pstack for the Copilot CLI and the GitHub Copilot app, which share ~/.copilot. Start a new session afterwards. Copilot ships no default pstack models, so the first skill that needs one runs setup-pstack to pick from the models your account lists, and later sessions reuse that choice.

The Copilot build is tested on Copilot CLI 1.0.87 through 1.0.92. On those versions the routing hook's context reaches the session alongside other plugins' session-start context. If a later version keeps only one plugin's context, setup-pstack offers a standing instruction for ~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md instead. On 1.0.92, once the CLI caches its computer-use experiment assignment, copilot -p sessions list no plugin skills and a skill call returns "Skill not found". Interactive sessions, the hooks, and the agents are unaffected.

Muse

Run in your terminal:

git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude
cd pstack-claude
muse plugins install ./plugins/pstack
muse plugins approve pstack

The first command installs the native Muse plugin bundle. The second approves its SessionStart hook and agent definitions, which Muse runs only after approval. Start a new session afterwards. Invoke a skill with /<name> (for example /poteto-mode), which Muse lists for each user-invocable skill.

OMP

Run in your terminal:

omp plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude
omp plugin install --scope user pstack@pstack-claude

Restart OMP after installing, disabling, or uninstalling pstack. OMP 18.16.0 shares one plugin cache across scopes, so an upgrade or removal can affect other installations; inspect their source and scope before changing them. See OMP issue 16827.

Kimi Code CLI

After a release containing kimi.plugin.json is published, close other Kimi sessions and install it in a fresh Kimi Code CLI session:

/plugins install https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude
/reload

To test an unreleased checkout, use /plugins install /absolute/path/to/pstack-claude instead, followed by /reload; Kimi copies the whole checkout, including Git metadata and local files, so use a clean, reviewed copy. To update, close other Kimi sessions, reinstall from the same source in a fresh session, and run /reload. Invoke a skill as /skill:pstack:poteto-mode; see the Kimi mapping for tool guidance.

Grok Build 
git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude
cd pstack-claude
grok plugin install "$PWD/plugins/pstack" --trust
grok plugin enable pstack

Start a new session and use /poteto-mode to load the skill explicitly. To update a local install, quit Grok sessions, inspect grok plugin details pstack and back up any edits in the installed copy, pull the checkout, run grok plugin uninstall pstack --keep-data, and repeat the last two commands. If pstack was disabled, disable it again before restarting. grok plugin update does not refresh a local install.

MiniMax Code

For a first install, check that ${MINIMAX_DATA_DIR:-$HOME/.minimax}/plugins/pstack does not already exist. Then run in your terminal:

git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude
cd pstack-claude
mkdir -p "${MINIMAX_DATA_DIR:-$HOME/.minimax}/plugins"
cp -R plugins/pstack "${MINIMAX_DATA_DIR:-$HOME/.minimax}/plugins/pstack"

MiniMax Code loads each directory under plugins/ in its data directory as a local plugin, and reads pstack through its Claude Code reader with the skills, agents, and routing hook. mcode plugin list shows it as pstack@local. To update, record its enabled state, quit every mcode process, and move plugins/pstack to an unused path outside plugins/. Run git pull and the cp line again. Check mcode plugin list and restore the previous enabled state if needed.

OpenCode 2

Clone the repository, then add the absolute path to plugins/pstack/opencode to the existing plugins array in ~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc. On Windows, use a path such as C:/Users/name/pstack-claude/plugins/pstack/opencode. Restart OpenCode after checkout updates.

Alternatively, install, check, or update the native Git package:

opencode plugin add 'github:michael-denyer/pstack-claude#main'
opencode plugin check 'github:michael-denyer/pstack-claude#main'
opencode plugin update 'github:michael-denyer/pstack-claude#main'

A commit-pinned reference does not advance. If a check immediately after installation reports no package plugins, wait for the server to load it and check again.

If you previously installed pstack skills into ~/.agents/skills, inspect the links and remove only those pointing to your pstack checkout before using the plugin.

The plugin registers pstack- skill IDs and adds routing in root sessions. If routing is missing, run opencode api get /api/skill and check that each pstack- path belongs to this plugin. Resolve any conflicting skill before manually invoking that ID. Use session hook: off in the OpenCode model sheet to disable routing. To remove the plugin, remove its configured path and restart the service, or use opencode plugin remove with the exact Git specifier. OpenCode 1 is unsupported. See the OpenCode mapping.

Antigravity (agy)

Run in your terminal:

git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude
cd pstack-claude
agy plugin install ./plugins/pstack

This installs the native Antigravity plugin bundle (skills, agents, and SessionStart routing hook) into ~/.gemini/config/plugins/pstack.

Other harnesses

Gemini CLI, Prime Agent, and skills-only Codex installs read skills from ~/.agents/skills/. Run in your terminal:

git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude
cd pstack-claude
mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills
for s in plugins/pstack/skills/*/; do
  target=~/.agents/skills/"$(basename "$s")"
  test -e "$target" || test -L "$target" || ln -s "$(pwd)/$s" "$target"
done

To update, run git pull in the clone, then run the for loop again to link skills added since the last run. These installs have no routing hook, so ask for poteto-mode by name or add a standing instruction to the harness's instruction file. See shared installation for per-harness notes and uninstalling.

Configure

pstack provides automatic routing on Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Muse, MiniMax Code, Antigravity, Pi, Kimi Code CLI, OMP, and OpenCode 2. The runtimes deliver the instruction at different points: Kimi adds it while the plugin is enabled, OMP adds it before each main-agent turn, and OpenCode adds it at each model step in root sessions. Grok Build exposes a routing hint through a skill description; the model may not follow it. Codex requires hook trust through /hooks, and Muse requires muse plugins approve pstack. Other harnesses have no automatic routing.

Run setup-pstack to turn automatic routing on or off, change model defaults, or set a reasoning effort per role (arena runners: opus @xhigh, fable @max). On OMP, the session hook setting applies globally across profiles; on Kimi, enable or disable the plugin to control routing. See the routing reference.

Getting started

Use poteto-mode to fix the search filter resetting when I change pages.

For a bug, it reproduces the failure, uses how and why to investigate, delegates the fix, then reruns the failing case. If the fix crosses a function boundary, it brings in architect before implementation. You receive the fix and the failing and passing evidence.

Other playbooks cover planning, features, refactoring, performance issues, investigations, prototypes, PR maintenance, shipping, and longer projects.

Details

  • Skills and slash commands
  • Runtime setup
  • Models and dependencies
  • Maintenance and port scope

Data handling

pstack has no server or telemetry. Anything its skills ask your agent to read, including session transcripts, goes to your model provider. Scripts run locally, and PR tools use your GitHub CLI login.

Contributing

Thanks for helping make this port better. Bug reports, documentation fixes, and runtime improvements are welcome. See CONTRIBUTING.md for the checks and where your change belongs. Report vulnerabilities privately as described in SECURITY.md.

To support maintenance of this port, buy the maintainer a coffee.

License

This port, including its modifications and additions, is also MIT-licensed, © 2026 Michael Denyer. Original pstack © 2026 Lauren Tan; imported cursor-team-kit and thermos skills © 2026 Cursor. See LICENSE-cursor-team-kit, LICENSE-thermos, and NOTICE.md.

aiSummary.oneLiner: An opinionated agent skill stack for Claude Code and Codex to improve autonomous workflows.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Pstack is a specialized plugin and skill stack designed to enhance the capabilities of AI coding harnesses like Claude Code and Codex. It ports rigorous, verified agent workflows originally designed for Cursor into other terminal-based AI environments. The tool manages named policy forks to enforce concise, simple, and secure coding practices during autonomous generation. By invoking specific workflows based on user goals, it significantly improves the reliability and outcome of agent-driven development tasks.
keyFeatures: Workflow translation: Ports Cursor-specific agent primitives to work seamlessly with Claude Code and Codex.
Policy management: Maintains named policy forks to enforce strict coding standards and behaviors.
Goal-oriented execution: Automatically invokes the correct operational workflow based on the stated task goal.
Code verification: Integrates strategies to ensure AI-generated code remains concise, simple, and secure.
Multi-harness support: Designed to operate across various agent environments including Pi and OpenCode.

useCases.title: Autonomous code generation
useCases.description: Improve the quality and reliability of code generated by terminal-based AI agents.

useCases.title: Enforcing project standards
useCases.description: Use named policy forks to ensure AI agents adhere to specific repository formatting and architectural rules.

useCases.title: Complex refactoring
useCases.description: Guide agents through rigorous workflows to safely refactor large sections of a codebase.

useCases.title: Cross-platform agent tooling
useCases.description: Standardize agent behaviors across different AI harnesses like Claude Code and Codex.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: This project is for developers and prompt engineers who actively use terminal-based AI coding assistants and want to enforce stricter, more reliable workflows. It requires familiarity with CLI agent tools.
